provenance: PR #29 R21. Three times in this PR a published wall-clock band failed to match the `evals/report/history.jsonl` committed beside it: nine of fifteen runs published as 'every run the ledger records', four values that appear in no recorded run at that case count, the two slowest `invariant` runs dropped unlabelled, and a ceiling derived from a maximum (64.71s) that was never measured. Nothing graded any of it, which is why prose drifted that far — and the same selective-band presentation is what ADR-013 Decision 4 was withdrawn over. This grades the PROPERTY, not the snapshot: `history.jsonl` grows on every gate run, so a check that string-matched the published list would go red on the next run rather than on a regression. It asserts that the doc's case count is the current one, that the committed ceiling is at least ADR-013's rule applied to the ledger's slowest run at that count, and that the published number derives that same ceiling. The last one is deliberately `rule(published) == rule(ledger max)` rather than the stricter `published >= ledger max` the reviewer proposed: the harmful failure R21 found is a band that justifies a LOWER ceiling than the truth (12.96s published where 13.57s was recorded, giving 15 where the rule said 20), and the strict form reddens on ordinary variance instead — this tree moved 0.2-0.5s between consecutive runs while the check was being written, which would make the doc need re-editing after every slightly slow run. That is the same rot-by-construction trap in a different place, so the property graded is the one that matters. T-R34 added two halves to the same check, both from the drift that produced that task: README's band-table row must carry the SAME case count and maximum as ADR-019's sentence (the two documents drifted apart in PR #29 R24 and only the ADR was graded), and a suite may publish exactly one band line -- the parse is a dict comprehension over `finditer`, so a superseded line left in the file used to shadow the live one in silence. PR #35 R2 and R4 added the two halves the round-1 version still missed: README's row parse was the same last-wins dict comprehension the ADR side had just been guarded against (stale rows ABOVE live rows left it green with two contradictory bands per suite), and nothing read the ceiling the ADR DERIVES in prose -- so a band re-measured downwards after a case was added could argue `-> **15**` under a heading that says 20s. The derivation sentence must now multiply the published maximum, be arithmetically right, and land on `WALL_BUDGET_S[suite]`. PR #35 R5 added the third: the published number must BE a row in the ledger recorded with nothing uncommitted in the tree (`dirty: false`). Round 1 published both bands off runs that were red AND dirty -- a band justified by a tree that was never committed. Green is deliberately NOT required and cannot be: this check is in both suites, so at a new case count every run is red until the band is republished and no green row could ever exist to republish it from (T-R42 carries that half). `evals/run.py` had to be fixed in the same round for a clean row to be producible at all -- `dirty` was read AFTER the report file was written, so every `--report` run recorded itself as dirty on account of its own untracked artifact.

triage.note: tagged invariant. The cost is deliberate and is the same one `docs-numbers-are-derived` charges: a run slower than the published band reddens the next gate run until the band is re-measured, and adding a case to a suite reddens it until the band is re-measured at the new count. A band nobody re-measures is the thing that produced R21.
triage.watched_red: three ways, each against the defect it rules out. (1) Against the text as PR #29 R21 found it — ADR-019 publishing `invariant` 12.96s and `fast` 64.71s — the check reports {suite: invariant, published_slowest: 12.96, ledger_slowest: 13.57, ceiling: 15, required_by_adr013_rule: 20} and {suite: fast, published_slowest: 64.71, ledger_slowest: 65.14}: a maximum that was in no recorded run, and a ceiling the rule had never justified. (2) With the committed `invariant` ceiling put back to 15 against the current ledger: {suite: invariant, ceiling: 15, required_by_adr013_rule: 20, ledger_slowest: 14.12}. (3) Before ADR-019 carried any band line at all: {suite: fast, adr_publishes_no_band_line: true} and the same for invariant. It also went red for real, unplanned, during this commit's own preparation: a 66.50s `fast` run landed after the band was published at 65.53s, and the next gate run reported it — which is the behaviour, not a defect. T-R34's two additions were watched red the same way: editing README's `fast` row to 66.05s against an ADR that says 66.38s gives {suite: fast, adr_band: [133, 66.38], readme_band: [133, 66.05]}; deleting README's `invariant` row gives {suite: invariant, adr_band: [52, 13.22], readme_band: null}; and adding a second `Slowest recorded `invariant` run at 52 cases` line gives {suite: invariant, adr_publishes_two_band_lines: true} plus the README disagreement the shadowing line caused. PR #35 R2/R4, three more, each the reviewer's own reproduction. Stale 132/66.33 and 51/14.12 rows inserted ABOVE README's live rows: [{suite: fast, readme_publishes_two_bands: true}, {suite: invariant, readme_publishes_two_bands: true}]. The band re-measured down to 12.80s with §3 and README following it: [{suite: invariant, published_slowest: 12.8, derives_ceiling: 15, ledger_slowest: 13.22, ledger_derives: 20, runs: 13}, {suite: invariant, derivation: [12.8, 14.7, 15], arithmetic: 14.7, committed_ceiling: 20}] -- the second entry is the new one, and it is the state R4 showed was reachable with everything else green. Breaking the arithmetic alone (`66.38 x 1.15 = 66.3`): [{suite: fast, derivation: [66.38, 66.3, 80], arithmetic: 76.3, committed_ceiling: 80}]. R5 watched red against exactly what round 1 shipped: republishing `invariant`'s band from ts 20260823-023204 (13.22s, `passed: 50, total: 52, dirty: true`) gives {suite: invariant, published: 13.22, is_not_a_clean_recorded_run_at: 52}.
